CONSENT CALENDAR
CCEA CC 1. Approve California Choice Energy Authority Entering into a Long-Term Energy Storage Resource Adequacy Agreement with Black Walnut Energy Storage, LLC on behalf of Pico Rivera Innovative Municipal Energy, Rancho Mirage Energy Authority and San Jacinto Power.
In November 2019, the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) approved Decision 19-11-016 (Decision) intended to address concerns that the state would have insufficient generation capacity resources beginning in summer 2021. The Decision requires all load serving entities, including Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) programs to procure 3300 MW of incremental resource adequacy. The Decision provides allocations for each load serving entity. Pico Rivera Innovative Municipal Energy (PRIME) was allocated 2.6 MW of additional month resource adequacy procurement; Rancho Mirage Energy Authority (RMEA) was allocated 4.8 MW of additional month resource adequacy procurement, and San Jacinto Power (SJP) was allocated 2.8 MW of additional monthly resource adequacy procurement. Additionally, the Decision requires that the contract term for contracts for each non-natural gas resource used to satisfy this requirement be 10 years or greater.

CC 4. Adopt Resolution No. 20-11, approving Senate Bill 1 (SB 1) Proposed Project List Form and allocate funds in the fiscal year 2020-2021 Capital Improvement Budget to clarify Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account (RMRA) funded projects.
The Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017, Senate Bill 1 (SB 1), was passed by the State Legislature and signed into law by the Governor in April 2017. The purpose of the bill is to help the State and local agencies address road maintenance. SB 1 will generate revenue through increases in gas tax, vehicle registration fees, and fees on zero emission vehicles. The tax and fee rate increases are implemented over time, beginning on November 1, 2017, with final implementation of all of the rate and fee increases in July 2020.

CC 5. Proposed Budget Transfers Between Capital Improvement Projects Previously Appropriated by Council in the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Five-Year Capital Improvement Program
a.
Approve a budget transfer from Capital Improvement Project 210-12ST036-924 (16/17 Pavement Management Program) in the amount of $200,000 to project 210-15SW016-924 (Pedestrian Gap Closure).
b.
Approve a budget transfer from Capital Improvement Project 210-15ST055-924 (5th Street East Corridor Improvements) in the amount of $100,000 to project 210-15SW016-924 (Pedestrian Gap Closure).
Capital Improvement Projects 210-12ST036-924 (16/17 Pavement Management Program) and 210-15ST055-924 (5th Street East Corridor Improvements) are coming to a close with approximately $300,000 in project savings. Project 210-15SW016-924 (Pedestrian Gap Closure) needs $300,000 in additional funding to cover anticipated right-of-way acquisition expenses. The Pedestrian Gap Closure project will install curb, gutter and sidewalk improvements at 37 separate locations within the City. The project is funded over multiple years, in part, with a Federal Active Transportation Program (ATP) grant. In order to meet the project delivery and timely use of funds requirements for the grant, the project schedule was accelerated and has advanced faster than funds were programmed. With approval of these budget transfers, program funding will be advanced, the project will continue to move forward and maintain the grant delivery schedule.

Award Public Works Construction Project No. 16-007, 2017 Traffic Signal Upgrades, to California Professional Engineering, Inc., of La Puente, California, in the amount of $524,628, base bid, plus a 15% of contingency, to add protected left-turn phasing to five existing signals locations. This contract is awarded to the lowest responsive bidder based on California Public Contract Code Section 22038 (b).
The City’s Traffic Engineering Section regularly surveys the City’s traffic signals. This includes both looking at traffic flow and traffic safety. Five locations were identified where adding protected left turns would increase both the traffic flow and safety of those locations: Milling Street/Lancaster Boulevard/Division Street; 10th Street West/Newgrove Avenue; 20th Street West/Avenue J-8; 17th Street East/Avenue J; and 27th Street West/Avenue J. The City subsequently hired a consultant traffic engineer to design the proposed improvements.

NEW BUSINESS
NB 1. “Stand Strong” Business Recovery Loan Program
Recommendations:
a.
Approve the City of Lancaster “Stand Strong” Business Recovery Loan Program to assist small businesses during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.
b.
Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute standard City agreements to issue loans to qualifying businesses of $5,000 - $20,000 per business, up to a total combined expenditure of $2,000,000. Under unique circumstances, the amount of the loan may be increased to suit a particular business’s needs, pending availability of funds and approval by the City Council.
c.
Appropriate $2,000,000 from General Fund account 101-2900-000, Fund Balance to account 101-4431-770, Stand Strong Business Recovery Loan Program.
With 14,631 confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the United States and 1,041 in California at the time of writing, governments across the country are taking decisive action to stop the spread of the coronavirus pandemic. On March 16, 2020, Los Angeles County mandated the closure of all bars, clubs, theaters, entertainment centers, and fitness centers until further notice. On March 19th, Governor Gavin Newsom mandated the closure of all “non-essential” businesses until further notice, while Los Angeles County issued the same mandate through April 19th. Restaurants are permitted to serve takeout or delivery food only. Clearly, such closures will have far-reaching impacts on the affected businesses, as well as on the local economy as a whole. To help combat these negative impacts and ensure business continuity and recovery, the City Council has directed staff to establish the “Stand Strong” Business Recovery Loan Program (Stand Strong). Stand Strong will allow for the issuance of loans ranging from $5,000 to $20,000 to businesses impacted by COVID-19, with first priority given to those directly affected by the closures. Under unique circumstances, the amount of the loan may be increased to suit the business’s needs, pending availability of funds and approval by the City Council.
